background: The Toronto-Dominion Bank is Canada's second-largest bank, funded by Canadian and US deposits and lending on Canadian mortgages and to businesses, with a large US retail bank along the east coast that has been under a regulatory asset cap after its anti-money-laundering failures.
synthesis: Ratings are A+ on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A, all three on a stable outlook, but the last move was a one-notch downgrade by one of them on 23 Oct 2024. Capital is strong: CET1 of 14.3% is in the top quarter of Canadian banks, though it has fallen 0.6 points since 30 Apr 2025 (figures to 31 Jul 2026). The profile carries no leverage or liquidity ratios, so capital is the only ratio to go on. Flagged items are operational and conduct matters — the newest, on 25 Sep 2026, a further disclosed customer data breach, alongside senior management turnover — the pattern a treasurer would expect while remediation continues.
